feat(loom-myhi.3): evidence-slot return contract on the four advice-producing agents

Realizes D1's scope for the non-dispatched half of the claim-provenance
epic (loom-myhi). Each of the four agents/*.md definitions that returns
advice central then acts on now carries the D2 evidence-slot contract:
every load-bearing claim carries either a citation (the command run and
its result, or a file:line) or the literal marker INFERRED.

The contract sentence is identical across all four; the sentence that
follows names each agent's own report shape:

- bug-family-researcher: binds lineage statements, KG facts, and every
  sentence of "Recommended approach" (the channel hooks/bd-claim-research.sh
  actively nudges central to dispatch while nothing checks it).
- project-onboarder: binds each verdict's rationale line; keeps the slot
  bracket separate from [AUTOFIX:<id>] so the skill's parse stays clean.
- drawer-author: binds ROOT CAUSE / WHAT SHIPPED / VERIFICATION /
  CALLER IMPACT; the "cite file:line whenever you can" style bullet now
  names INFERRED as the other branch.
- kg-relationship-extractor: adds an `evidence:` field to the triple
  template; *Why* keeps the reasoning, evidence: says where it was read.

A citation is a POINTER, not a rationale (Bucinca et al., CSCW 2021 —
explanations do not reduce overreliance). No confidence field, no
certainty score, no trust rating: all three are in the epic's YAGNI cut.

Scope held to D1: central's own claims to the user and human-reviewer
advice stay out — central has no transcript-reader over itself, and
mixing an unenforceable clause into an enforceable rule dilutes the gate.

Design doc: drawer_loom_decisions_1a296178707cdc55c872b467

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NbfeEwpYnAePZCACVj3Ctd
EOF

content.text:
Done. Report follows, under the contract this bead is building.

## 1. What was added, with insertion points

All four received one `## Evidence slot (required) — loom-myhi` section; two also received an in-template touch.

- **`agents/bug-family-researcher.md:55`** — section inserted between the "If searches return nothing relevant…" line and `## Do NOT`. Plus **line 44**: appended `Every claim here carries an evidence slot (see below).` to the `## Recommended approach` template line — the sharpest channel, since `hooks/bd-claim-research.sh` nudges central to dispatch this agent on every claim. `[grep -n "Evidence slot" agents/bug-family-researcher.md → 55]`
- **`agents/project-onboarder.md:352`** — section inserted after the `### AUTOFIX tags on suggested-fix lines` subsection, before `## Do NOT`. `[grep -n → 352]`
- **`agents/drawer-author.md:80`** — section inserted between `## Output format` and `## Style rules`. Plus **line 93**: the style bullet `Cite file:line whenever you can.` now reads `… — where you cannot, mark the claim INFERRED (see Evidence slot).` `[grep -n → 80, 93]`
- **`agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md:51`** — section inserted after the "Cap at 5 triples" line, before `## Style rules`. Plus **line 35**: an `evidence: <command + result, or file:line, or INFERRED>` field added to the triple template. `[grep -n → 35, 51]`

## 2. Exact wording

The contract sentence is **byte-identical in all four files**:

> Every load-bearing claim carries either a citation — the command you ran and its result, or a `file:line` — or the literal marker `INFERRED`. A citation is a pointer, not a rationale: it says where to look, not why to believe.

What differs is the **one sentence after it**, which names each agent's own report shape (this is the D1/D2 "worded for each agent's own report shape" requirement):

- bug-family-researcher: `This binds every lineage statement, every KG fact, and every sentence of **Recommended approach**. Citations do not count toward the 400-word cap.`
- project-onboarder: `This binds each verdict's rationale line. Every item's scan recipe names a probe, so INFERRED should be rare here — reach for it when a verdict rests on reading rather than running.` Plus a closing line: `Keep the slot and the [AUTOFIX:<id>] tag as separate brackets, never nested, so the skill's literal-substring parse stays clean.`
- drawer-author: `This binds ROOT CAUSE, WHAT SHIPPED, VERIFICATION, and CALLER IMPACT. The main agent files this drawer as the project's record, so a claim you could not ground must say so.`
- kg-relationship-extractor: `Each triple's evidence: field is that slot, and so is each entry under Invalidations to consider. *Why* still carries the reasoning; evidence: says where the relationship was read from.`

Each section closes with a 3-line example in the agent's own idiom (one citation-by-command, one `file:line`, one `INFERRED`). No confidence field, certainty score, or trust rating was added anywhere. `[git diff --stat main HEAD → 4 files, 46 insertions, 2 deletions]`

## 3. Diff + SHA

```
 agents/bug-family-researcher.md     | 12 +++++++++++-
 agents/drawer-author.md             | 12 +++++++++++-
 agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md | 11 +++++++++++
 agents/project-onboarder.md         | 13 +++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 46 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```
Commit `10adb80a77123f4df051ffb0b815f9d2843bcb10` on `frank/loom-myhi.3`. Not pushed, not merged, bead not closed. Working tree clean. `[git status --porcelain → empty]`

## 4. Footprint expansion

**None** — exactly the four declared `Files:`. `.beads/issues.jsonl` was dirtied by `bd update --claim` and was **restored, not committed** (`git checkout -- .beads/issues.jsonl`), per the worktree bd-state convention. `[git status --porcelain after restore → only the 4 agent files]`

## 5. Processed

4 of 4 files. No sampling.

## 6. Uncertain / judgment calls

- **`[INFERRED]` — the word-cap carve-out.** I added `Citations do not count toward the 400-word cap.` to bug-family-researcher. This rule is **not in the design doc**; I inferred it because the file's hard 400-word cap and the new mandatory slot are in direct tension — without the carve-out, the cap squeezes out exactly the thing D2 requires. project-onboarder needed no analogue (its cap is 250 *lines*, and slots ride on existing lines). If central disagrees, deleting that one sentence is the whole revert.
- **`[INFERRED]` — the `— loom-myhi` heading suffix.** project-onboarder cites lineage pervasively; the other three cite none. I put the marker on all four for uniformity and so a reader has a route to the design. Cheap to strip.
- **`[INFERRED]` — the drawer-author style-bullet edit** (`agents/drawer-author.md:93`) is the one change beyond pure addition. `Cite file:line whenever you can.` sitting next to a mandatory contract is a latent inconsistency, so I made the bullet name `INFERRED` as the other branch. This is a 1-line judgment, not something the bead asked for.
- **Where the shape fit worst: `kg-relationship-extractor`.** Its output is triples, not prose claims, and it *already* has a `*Why*` line — so the risk was the slot collapsing into the rationale, which is precisely what D2 forbids. I resolved it by making `evidence:` a separate template field and stating the division explicitly (`*Why*` = reasoning, `evidence:` = where it was read). This is the only one of the four where the contract needed a structural field rather than a prose convention. `[agents/kg-relationship-extractor.md:35,53]`
- **Not verified: the T1 reader's parse shape.** `loom-myhi.1` (the transcript reader) is still in progress by another worker, so I could not check that my bracket convention (`[citation]` / `[INFERRED]`, and kg's bare `evidence:` field) is what the reader will actually recognize. `[INFERRED]` — I matched the design doc's example syntax verbatim, but the kg `evidence:`-field form is a shape the drawer does not show. Worth a cross-check when T1 lands.

## Verification run (targeted only; no `script/test`)

`drawer-author-guest.test.sh` 6/0 · `audit-rules-no-autofix.test.sh` 11/0 · `audit-check4-delegates.test.sh` 14/0 · `audit-script-convention.test.sh` 34/0 · `scripts/loom-docs-catalogue --check` OK (59 primitives) · `scripts/loom-docs-gen --check` OK. `[each command's tail output, above]` The docs engines catalogue agents by filename and front-matter `description`, neither of which I touched — so no nav regeneration is implied.
